chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Jamilah, from Sindī, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the woman who is a follower of the school of the Prophet's family (Ahl al-Bayt), asking if she should be married to the Nāsib (one who is hostile to them). He said, 'No, because the Nāsib is a disbeliever.' I said, 'Then should she be married to a man who is neither a Nāsib nor a follower of the school?' He said, 'The one who is neither is more beloved to me than the one who is a follower.'

key_terms.النَّاصِبَ: The Nāsib (one hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.الْعَارِفَةِ: The woman who is knowledgeable/follower of the Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred marital status for a woman who is a follower of the Ahl al-Bayt regarding a Nāsib or a neutral man?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the criterion for prohibiting marriage to a Nāsib is explicitly defined as kufr (disbelief), elevating the status of the Ahl al-Bayt's enemies to that of non-believers in the context of marital compatibility. The Imam’s preference for a man who is 'neither Nāsib nor Arif' highlights the Shia jurisprudential nuance that while loyalty to the Ahl al-Bayt is ideal, a neutral believer is preferable to a specific follower who might lack broader religious grounding, emphasizing practical social harmony over rigid sectarian labeling.
